metaData.originalTitle: Formal methods and the future of programming
metaData.title: Formal methods and the future of programming
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Jane Street shifts from skepticism to excitement about formal methods, driven by agentic coding's potential to lower costs and increase benefits, and is building a dedicated team.
metaData.summary: This article from Jane Street's engineering blog announces a significant strategic shift: the company is now building a team focused on formal methods after 25 years of skepticism. The author explains that the emergence of agentic coding has fundamentally changed the cost/benefit calculus. On the cost side, AI models make formal methods easier to use, broadening the pool of productive users. On the benefit side, the 'verification bottleneck' created by AI-generated code (which tends to be 'slop') is more critical than ever, and formal methods can provide powerful feedback for AI agents. The article argues that Jane Street is uniquely positioned due to its deep control over its in-house language, OxCaml, and a community of programmers eager for advanced type-system features. It concludes with a call for applications for formal methods experts in London and New York.

mainPoints.point: Agentic coding changes the cost/benefit calculus for formal methods.
mainPoints.explanation: AI models lower the cost of using formal methods by automating drudgery and broadening access, while simultaneously increasing the benefit by creating a verification bottleneck for AI-generated code.

mainPoints.point: Formal methods are a powerful form of feedback for AI agents.
mainPoints.explanation: Agents thrive on feedback, and formal methods provide universal guarantees (like type safety) that are more powerful than testing alone for catching bugs and improving code quality.

mainPoints.point: Jane Street is uniquely positioned to advance this field.
mainPoints.explanation: The company has deep control over its language (OxCaml) and a community of programmers who are already demanding and using advanced type-system features, providing an ideal testing ground.

keyQuotes: I've been telling people for the last 25 years that Jane Street as an organization was just not interested in formal methods. I'm not saying that anymore.
Our hope is to make formal methods as pervasively useful of a tool for building software as sophisticated type systems are for us today.
Agentic code is getting better, but is still tends towards slop: overly complicated, full of weird bugs and corner cases, often not following essential invariants of the codebase that it's a part of.

relatedArticles.title: Harness design for long-running application development
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article explores Anthropic's multi-agent harness design (Planner, Generator, Evaluator) for long-running autonomous coding, detailing how to overcome context anxiety and self-evaluation bias to build complex full-stack applications.

relatedArticles.title: Xiaomi MiMo， Explore and Love
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Xiaomi MiMo and TileRT achieve 1000+ tokens/s inference on a 1-trillion-parameter model using commodity GPUs through extreme model-system codesign, including FP4 quantization and DFlash speculative decoding.

relatedArticles.title: Martin Fowler & Kent Beck: Frameworks for reinventing software， again and again
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Software legends Martin Fowler and Kent Beck discuss how AI redefines software engineering, emphasizing that core practices like TDD and modularity remain essential for human-AI collaboration.

relatedArticles.title: Inside FAISS: Billion-Scale Similarity Search
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a deep, visual, and intuitive explanation of FAISS, covering the core ideas of IVF, Product Quantization, their combination in IVFPQ, and GPU acceleration, to enable billion-scale similarity search.

relatedArticles.title: Cursor and SpaceX Partner to Scale AI Coding with Stargate-Class Infrastructure
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Cursor CEO Michael Truell announces a strategic partnership with SpaceX to leverage massive compute infrastructure for scaling the Cursor Composer and building advanced coding models.

relatedArticles.title: Harness engineering: leveraging Codex in an agent-first world
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI engineers detail a five-month experiment building a production software product with zero manually-written code, using Codex agents to achieve 10x velocity and redefining the engineer's role as system designer and feedback loop architect.

relatedArticles.title: Introducing Claude Opus 4.7
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Anthropic has released Claude Opus 4.7, a significant upgrade over Opus 4.6 with major improvements in advanced software engineering, vision capabilities, instruction following, and autonomous long-horizon reasoning, while implementing new cyber safeguards and maintaining the same pricing.

relatedArticles.title: Software Architecture Guide
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This page from Martin Fowler presents his perspective on software architecture, defining it as the important stuff in system design, and serves as a curated guide to his site's extensive resources on application and enterprise architecture.

relatedArticles.title: Andrej Karpathy on Code Agents， AutoResearch， and the Loopy Era of AI
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Andrej Karpathy explores the paradigm shift from manual programming to agent orchestration, the automation of AI research, and the profound implications for software engineering and education.

relatedArticles.title: Dario Amodei — Policy on the AI Exponential
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Dario Amodei argues that AI is advancing exponentially, creating a dangerous mismatch with slow-moving policy, and proposes concrete actions across regulation, economics, science, civil liberties, and geopolitics to meet the moment.
